findings.text: baseline_suite is a targeted 61-id run (40 failed / 21 passed in 344 s) while after_suite is the whole suite (9100 tests, 1842 s), so added_failure_ids compares two different populations; all 21 added ids were in the base arm and passed there, so each pass->fail move is real, but the base arm's load is not the whole-suite load the head run carried, which is why the 'load-only' cause for 20 of the 21 rests on a separate isolation recheck rather than on like-for-like arms.

after_suite.revision is b62d9fde, the parent of the reviewed head 5ab11b97 (the intervening commit is docs/evidence only), so the stored after-arm ties the gate to a tree one commit behind the head a reader selects the record by; and the declared after_suite.command omits the --timeout=300 that the head arm actually passed (run_head_arm.sh line 19), so it is not the literal command that ran.

the tests: field carries unsubstituted placeholders (<worktree>, <run>, <pid>), which the manifest contract forbids; the literal commands are only in baseline_suite/after_suite, and even there the after_suite command is missing the --timeout=300 the run used.

the guard has no committed test that makes it fire: its refusal is demonstrated only by a scratch-tree manual revert (negative-control.log) and by tests/test_crew_placed_liveness.py reaching squeue; the changed test file only provides a recording scheduler to one test, so a future edit could disable the session stub without any red test.

the session guard's own design turns a previously-green out-of-scope test red at head - tests/test_crew_placed_liveness.py::test_the_payload_log_decides_that_the_work_ran now ERRORS at teardown naming a refused 'squeue -h -j 1274000 -o %T' - a correct refusal of a real reach, but the node leaves it red and records only the one-line fix as a follow-on, so the node's own change is the cause of one of its 21 added failures.

justifications.durability: The guarded thing is made to happen and the refusal is shown: the negative control (logs/negative-control.log) reverts the recording scheduler in a scratch tree at head, and the conftest fixture fires naming the refused salloc argv while the same call also raises CrewError ('salloc answered no job identifier (exit 1)'), and I reproduced the guard firing live on a real squeue reach at head. The base arm shows the real allocation argv the instrument observes, so the guard demonstrably closes a hazard that had actually occurred. Docked two: no committed test asserts the fixture fires - its firing is shown only by a scratch-tree manual revert and by a pre-existing test's unintended reach, so a later edit could disable the stub without any red test; and the 20 load-only ids are attributed to load from a single isolation recheck rather than the plan section 3 measure's three consecutive -n 8 full-file runs, so load versus order dependence is not separated.
justifications.evidence: added_failure_count 21 and added_failure_ids are derived cleanly from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite and after_suite objects (both completed, both carry revision, command, exit_status, failure_count, failure_ids); absent is 0 (all 40 base failures persist at head). All 21 added ids were present in the base arm's command and passed there (61 ids: 40 failed, 21 passed), so the pass->fail move is real, not a set artefact. Docked three: (a) baseline_suite is a targeted 61-id run (344 s) at 008a18f1 while after_suite is the whole 9,100-test suite (1842 s) at b62d9fde, so the arms are not like-for-like populations and the 'load-only' cause for 20 of the 21 rests on a corroborating isolation recheck rather than on comparable arms; (b) after_suite.revision b62d9fde is the reviewed head's parent - head 5ab11b97 is a docs/evidence commit on top - so the after arm ties the gate to a tree one docs commit behind the head the record is selected by; (c) after_suite.command omits the --timeout=300 that the head arm actually passed (run_head_arm.sh line 19 and the run line in the log), so the declared command is not the literal command that ran.
justifications.fit: The change follows repository idioms: the conftest fixture builds its stub under tmp_path_factory, the changed test keeps its hermetic temp RECKON_HOME and synthesised cgroup tree, and PATH prepending with restore is the established pattern. No plan label, version, ticket or author reference appears in any staged path, symbol or comment; the comments explain the mechanism (why a forgotten scheduler lets a real allocation be minted). Docked one because the new conftest comment carries a measurement date and incident narrative ('measured 2026-09-30, an admitted-dispatch case minted a real allocation'), which is changelog prose rather than the guard's own mechanism.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's stated goal - a whole-suite run cannot reach the real scheduler - is met and independently reproduced. At the reviewed head a session autouse conftest fixture puts a refusing stub for salloc/sbatch/srun/squeue/scontrol/scancel first on PATH, and the changed test now provides its own recording scheduler so the admitted-dispatch case's ensure is intercepted. I ran tests/test_concurrency_bound_refuses_by_name.py at 5ab11b97: 3 passed, EXIT=0; and I reproduced the guard refusing a live reach myself by running tests/test_crew_placed_liveness.py::test_the_payload_log_decides_that_the_work_ran at head, which errors at teardown with 'this test reached a scheduler verb it did not provide: squeue -h -j 1274000 -o %T'. The head whole-suite run's reach log (logs/reach-head.tsv) carries exactly one line, a refused squeue, and no salloc or sbatch, and the base arm (logs/shim-base.tsv) shows the same instrument DID observe the real 'salloc --no-shell --job-name=reckon-reservation --partition=all --cpus-per-task=32 --mem=128G' before the fix - a positive control that the absence at head is meaningful. Docked one because the guard's own design turns a previously-green out-of-scope test red
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 008a18f1 5ab11b97 shows exactly two changed files, tests/conftest.py and tests/test_concurrency_bound_refuses_by_name.py, both inside the node's declared write paths; the docs/evidence fragment sits in its own commit b62d9fde..5ab11b97. The worker committed locally, pushed nothing, and did not mutate the plan, project index or sprint state (the landing record is the coordinator's to write). The worktree is clean at 5ab11b97 and no figure was produced at the declared docs/figures path, which for a test-infrastructure guard is a reasonable omission rather than a defect.
